title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 6 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

questions.prompt: Name the green pigment that traps light energy in leaves.
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is found in the chloroplasts.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide enters through the stomata.

questions.prompt: What are the products of photosynthesis?
Plants respire only at night.
questions.explanation: Plants respire all the time, day and night.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its description.

pairs.right: Pores that let gases in and out of a leaf

questions.prompt: Give TWO differences between photosynthesis and respiration.
questions.memo:
Any two, 2 marks each (both sides of the difference):
✓✓ Photosynthesis uses CO₂ and water; respiration uses glucose and oxygen
✓✓ Photosynthesis happens only in light; respiration happens all the time
✓✓ Photosynthesis takes place in chloroplasts; respiration in mitochondria
✓✓ Photosynthesis stores energy; respiration releases energy

questions.prompt: Explain why photosynthesis is important for animals, even though animals do not photosynthesise.
questions.memo:
✓ Plants are the start of food chains, so animals get their food energy from plants (directly or indirectly) (1)
✓ Photosynthesis releases the oxygen animals need for respiration (1)

questions.prompt: What is the name for an organism that makes its own food?
In a food chain, the arrow points from the organism that is eaten to the organism that eats it.
questions.explanation: Arrows show the direction in which energy flows.

questions.prompt: Match each organism to its role.
Plants in a food chain store 50 000 kJ of energy. Using the 10% rule, how much energy is passed on to the herbivores?
Oxpeckers eat ticks off a buffalo's back. What kind of relationship is this?
questions.explanation: The bird gets food and the buffalo loses its ticks, so both benefit.

questions.prompt: What term describes all the organisms of one species living in an area?
Explain why there are usually fewer lions than zebras in a game reserve.
questions.memo:
✓ Only about 10% of energy passes from one trophic level to the next (energy is lost as heat and used for life processes) (1)
✓ So there is much less energy available at the top of the food chain, which can support only a few carnivores (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how alien invasive plants threaten South African ecosystems.
questions.memo:
✓ They use large amounts of water / spread quickly (1)
✓ and crowd out indigenous plants, so the animals that depend on those plants lose food and shelter (1)

questions.prompt: What is the scientific name for a micro-organism that causes disease?
Antibiotics can be used to cure flu, which is caused by a virus.
How is malaria spread?
Match each example to its group.
Pasteurisation preserves milk by…
Explain why bread dough rises when yeast is added.
questions.memo:
✓ Yeast feeds on sugar in the dough / respires (1)
✓ It produces carbon dioxide gas (1)
✓ The gas is trapped as bubbles, making the dough expand (1)

questions.prompt: Give THREE ways in which micro-organisms are useful to people.
questions.memo:
Any three (1 each):
✓ making food (bread, yoghurt, cheese, amasi)
✓ decomposing dead material / recycling nutrients
✓ making medicines (antibiotics, vaccines)
✓ helping digestion
✓ treating sewage

questions.prompt: What is the charge on an electron?
An oxygen atom has 8 protons. How many electrons does a neutral oxygen atom have?
Which of the following is a compound?
questions.explanation: Water is H₂O: hydrogen and oxygen chemically bonded. Air and salt water are mixtures.

questions.prompt: How many atoms in total are in one molecule of sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄?
Elements in Group 18 (the noble gases) are very reactive.
Match each element to its symbol.
Give THREE differences between a mixture and a compound.
questions.memo:
Any three (1 each):
✓ In a compound the elements are chemically bonded; in a mixture they are not
✓ A compound has a fixed composition; a mixture's composition can vary
✓ A compound can only be separated by chemical means; a mixture by physical means
✓ A compound has different properties from its elements; a mixture keeps the properties of its parts

sections.title: QUESTION 5: The Particle Model of Matter

questions.prompt: In which state do particles only vibrate in fixed positions?
What is the change of state from gas to liquid called?
What is the name for the spreading of particles from a high to a low concentration?
When a metal rod expands, its particles become bigger.
questions.explanation: The particles move further apart; they do not change size.

questions.prompt: A stone has a mass of 270 g and a volume of 100 cm³. Calculate its density.
Match each change of state to what happens.
Use the particle model to explain why gaps are left between sections of a railway line.
questions.memo:
✓ On hot days the particles in the steel gain energy and move/vibrate faster (1)
✓ They move further apart, so the steel expands (1)
✓ Without gaps the rails would push against each other and buckle (1)

questions.prompt: What is an insoluble solid that forms when two solutions react called?
In a chemical reaction, new atoms are created.
56 g of iron reacts completely with sulfur to form 88 g of iron sulfide. What mass of sulfur reacted?
In the equation CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O, how many oxygen atoms are on the product side?
questions.explanation: CO₂ has 2 and 2H₂O has 2, so 4 in total.

questions.prompt: Which observation does NOT necessarily show that a chemical reaction has taken place?
options: Bubbles of a new gas form
A solid changes shape when cut

questions.prompt: Match each observation to the sign of a chemical reaction it shows.

pairs.left: Fizzing when vinegar is added to baking soda
A cloudy solid appears when two clear solutions are mixed
A copper roof slowly turns green

questions.prompt: A learner says that mass is lost when paper burns because the ash is lighter than the paper. Explain why this is incorrect.
questions.memo:
✓ Gases (carbon dioxide and water vapour) are produced and escape into the air (1)
✓ The total mass of all products equals the mass of the reactants (paper + oxygen); mass is conserved (1)
